### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that the issue still exists on the latest versions of the docs on `main` [here](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/)


### Location of the documentation

pandas.Series.first_valid_index
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/ba1cccd19da778f0c3a7d6a885685da16a072870/pandas/core/generic.py#L12341

### Documentation problem

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/ba1cccd19da778f0c3a7d6a885685da16a072870/pandas/core/generic.py#L12341
The "Notes" passage reads: "If all elements are non-NA/null, returns None. Also returns None for empty Series/DataFrame."
but the "non-" should not be there.

### Suggested fix for documentation

The "non-" should be deleted from the "Notes" section, resulting in this:
"If all elements are NA/null, returns None. Also returns None for empty Series/DataFrame."
comments:
My understanding:
- The function is trying to return the first valid (i.e. non-NA and non-null) index in the series/frame
- The [docs](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/ba1cccd19da778f0c3a7d6a885685da16a072870/pandas/core/generic.py#L12341) say that if all elements are `non-NA/null, returns None`, which would imply that we would return `None` if all elements _are_ `non-null`, which I believe was not the intent

I will update this to remove the "non-" from that line. Thanks!

review_comments: Could you just remove this `Notes` section and demonstrate these points in the `Examples` section below?

Done. One thing I was unsure of was how to handle returning `None` in the docs:
- I ran it through the docstring validation script `python scripts/validate_docstrings.py pandas.core.generic.NDFrame.first_valid_index`
- It was throwing errors about the output not matching the expected output because I had originally specified:
```
        >>> s = pd.Series()
        >>> s.first_valid_index()
        None
        >>> s.last_valid_index()
        None
```

I considered printing the outputs so that the outputs would match but didn't see print statements used in that way in other parts of the code so I did not keep them. Let me know if printing is the way to go here and I can make the change :)

To clarify, option 1:
```
>>> s = pd.Series()
>>> s.first_valid_index()
>>> s.last_valid_index()
```

Option 2:
```
>>> s = pd.Series()
>>> print(s.first_valid_index())
None
>>> print(s.last_valid_index())
None
```
Option 2 would be fine to make it explicit in the docs
